title: Rename one stable Project without changing its Client relationship

requirements.invariant: A rename targets one existing stable ProjectID in one immutable Account and cannot change, infer or authorize its required ClientID relationship from Project or Client display text.

RenameProject is a distinct command over one validated nonblank current Project display name. It is not UpdateProjectDetails, RenameClient, ArchiveProject, ConfigureProjectCategories or ChangeProjectClient; duplicate display names cannot merge identity or enable Transfer.

RenameProject expresses one business intent through typed Ledger values and exposes no arbitrary field map, collection/path/SQL string, generic CRUD, Client, description, category, media, lifecycle, child, accounting or history mutation.

The Project rename payload is bound to exactly one OperationID, contract version, AccountID, actor PrincipalID and finite client-created time through the shared operation fingerprint and receipt lifecycle; rename defines no competing queue, retry, result or rejection semantics.

Rename carries exactly one expected-revision precondition for the same Project subject so stale intent cannot silently become last-write-wins; local construction records the precondition but does not decide authoritative conflict or idempotent-already-applied results.

requirements.section: Clients, Projects, notes, preferences, and reference data
requirements.invariant: One narrow backend-neutral Project rename operation accepts the validated command and returns the shared OperationReceipt or a stable failure; local validation never substitutes for trusted membership, Project existence/revision or mutation authorization at the later server boundary.

This Phase 1 command boundary is executable only with deterministic provider-free evidence while the shipped app remains unchanged and no Project table/handler, RLS policy, Sync Stream, Auth/provider choice, source transform, hosted resource or production authority is introduced.

items: ProjectRenameDraft owns exact Account, actor, operation-contract, stable Project, validated replacement ProjectDisplayName, ExpectedProjectRevision and finite capture time; it contains no Client/description/category/media/lifecycle/child/accounting/history input.

RenameProjectPayload contains only stable ProjectID and ProjectDisplayName. RenameProjectCommand binds it to the shared OperationEnvelope, derives the exact Project subject, requires exactly one same-subject expected-revision precondition and revalidates payload, subject, precondition and fingerprint on decode.

ProjectRenaming is the narrow backend-neutral operation port returning the shared OperationReceipt. Command receipt validation requires the exact OperationID and exposes no authoritative Project-row or downstream-projection result claim.

ProjectRenameFailure exposes stable bounded time, binding, revision-precondition, subject, fingerprint, receipt, local-acceptance and malformed-encoding codes while reusing verified ProjectDisplayName, ExpectedProjectRevision and shared operation validators.

items: The complete command is canonical Codable evidence over draft, shared envelope, Project subject and fingerprint; decode reconstructs through the same validators and byte-identical structured restart is required.
Changed Account, actor, contract, Project, name, revision, subject, preconditions, fingerprint or receipt OperationID fails atomically without rebinding identity or returning a partial command.

A deterministic reference adapter may accept the command into the shared OperationJournal and prove exact replay/receipt semantics; this is not physical durable-store, process/device restart, optimistic Project display or authoritative server apply evidence.

storageMedia.notApplicable: Project rename owns no attachment reference, local media receipt, bytes, upload, retention, deletion or presentation behavior and cannot replace hero media.

appMcp.notApplicable: No Project editor/list/detail/search view, current app service, MCP tool/schema, transport, contract-catalog entry or app/MCP parity claim is wired.

migrationReconciliation.notApplicable: No Firebase Project/name/clientName, report/Invoice display, source export or migration row is decoded or transformed. Later migration must preserve stable Project identity and intentional historical snapshots separately.

observabilityRunbooks.notApplicable: Stable local failures are contract values only; no signal emission, metric, alert, audit sink or runbook action is introduced.

items: Implementation remains inside provider-free LedgerTargetCore and its tests and does not change or link either application project.

The slice cannot rename a visible or authoritative Project, change Client relationship, description, category, media, lifecycle, children, accounting or historical evidence, authorize membership, define provider/schema/migration behavior, activate a feature, deploy, release or cut over.

verification.expected: A valid synthetic draft produces one typed exact-scope RenameProject command with one same-subject expected revision; the payload contains only stable Project identity and validated new display text and cannot carry Client, description, category, media, lifecycle, child, accounting or historical input.

Representative rename commands round-trip byte-identically with exact Account/actor/contract/Operation/Project/name/revision/time/subject/fingerprint evidence and no backend path, provider, credential, Client relationship, downstream projection or server-result claim.

Blank display text, invalid time and changed Account/actor/contract/Project/name/revision/payload/subject/preconditions/fingerprint/receipt evidence fail atomically through existing or Project-rename stable diagnostic codes.

A deterministic reference port returns the shared queued receipt, exact replay returns the same receipt, the same OperationID with changed Project/name/revision is refused by the shared lifecycle, and a failing port returns no success receipt.

notes: Decision-independent Phase 1 command boundary only. O-024/O-025 remain fully open because no lifecycle/delete/Client-reassignment behavior exists. The slice stops before physical durable storage, authoritative Project/downstream projection, server apply, schema/RLS/Sync/Auth/provider, app/MCP, source migration, hosted resources, production access or cutover.
